title: Theorem Of The Alternative
body_html:
Theorem Of The Alternative

Let $A$ be an $m\times n$ real matrix and let $b\in\mathbb R^m$. Define $$ S=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\ge b\} $$ and $$ T=\{u\in\mathbb R^m:u\ge 0,\ uA=0,\ \langle u,b\rangle>0\}. $$ Then exactly one of $S$ and $T$ is nonempty.

References

  • [MFoGT, Section 2.8, Exercise 7] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory, references/MechDesign.pdf. Fourier elimination theorem of the alternative.
